sets.group: O/qr-scanner (scanning-native, scanning-web, torch-on, permission) · O/browser-consent (favicon, fallback-logo) · O/browser-error (default)
sets.summary:
Seven planned cells; **zero** are capturable by the harness as it stands, for two completely different reasons — and the split matters.

**O/browser-consent (2) and O/browser-error (1) are impossible on web, permanently.** `src/modules/webview/index.tsx:31` sets `isWalletWebViewSupported = Platform.OS === 'ios' || Platform.OS === 'android'`, and `src/app/browser.tsx:364` returns `<Fallback>{t('connect.browser.unsupported')}</Fallback>` *before* the consent `AppModal` (line 498) or the `errorOverlay` (line 415) are ever in the tree. Both states of the consent sheet are chosen by `nav?.favicon`, and the error overlay by `nav?.error` — `nav` is only ever set by `onNavigationChange`, an event the native WebView emits and the web build cannot. There is no dev seam: `window.vela` carries only RPC/price/funding/gas faults. I captured the route to prove it; the dump is one text node.

**O/qr-scanner is a harness gap, not a platform limit — and it is a gap of exactly the class this project already got burned by.** The scanner is a raw react-native `<Modal>`, not an `AppModal`: on RNW it portals to a body-level wrapper *outside* the 390px `#root` frame, nested under two zero-size divs (0×0 and 1280×0). `extract-dom-layout.js:154` prunes anything below `minSize` **before** descending, so the entire overlay is dropped. The failure mode is the dangerous one: the scanner's text lives in `document.body.innerText`, so `expect: ["Scan QR"]` passes with confidence while the dump is a picture of Home. The `differsFrom` guard caught it — same fingerprint, `adc6bd013e40967b-53`.

Three prerequisites, each measured, all in the spec's `$requires`:
1. **`capture-states.js:352` must forward per-state extract options** — `window.extractLayout(st.extract)`. `{minSize: 0}` alone is enough; no edit to the extractor is needed (a `display:contents`-style pass-through for zero-size wrappers is cleaner and drops 42 empty nodes).
2. **`run-capture.mjs` needs a per-group `viewport`.** The modal is `position:fixed` to the *window*, so at 1280×950 it lands at (-445,-53) 1280×950: close button (-429,-33), torch (731,-33), hint y=861 — everything but the centred reticle falls outside the 390×844 board. At 390×844 the `min-width:500px` phone-frame rule in `src/global.css:81` doesn't apply, `#root` is full-bleed, and the same overlay comes out exactly `[0 0 390 844]`.
3. **chromium needs `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream` + camera permission.** The torch button only renders after `cameraReady` (`QRScanner.tsx:507`); with no device, `getUserMedia` rejects into an empty `.catch` and the header comes back with close + image-picker only — a board silently missing an affordance. The fake stream paints nothing (the `<video>` dumps as an empty box), so it costs the board nothing.

Two corrections to the brief: the scanner is **not** reachable from the in-app browser (that route has no scanner); its entries are the Home dock FAB (`aria-label "Scan"`), Send → enter-details (`"Scan a QR code"`), the Connections-tab Connect CTA, the WalletPair connect screen, and `AddTokenPanel`. And `dark: true` must **not** be set on these boards even though the scanner is pure black — the theme guard measures inside the phone frame, and the scanner is outside it.

One board worth adding that the manifest does not plan: `O/qr-scanner/web-camera-denied` — on web there is no permission screen at all, so a refused camera is simply the black viewfinder with the torch affordance gone. That is the honest web analogue of the native `permission` state, and it needs prerequisite 1+2 but not 3.

**1. /browser on web is a dead end — `node run-capture.mjs --dir _probe --url "/browser?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.uniswap.org" --slug _probe-browser-route --settle 6000`** → captured, 390×844. The entire dump:
```

    · [0 0 390 844]
      'The in-app browser is only available on iOS and Android.' [24 414 341 16]
  ... (7 empty siblings)
· [-445 -53 1280 950]
```
One text node. No top bar, no consent sheet, no error overlay. `/Volumes/data/production/vela-wallet/specs/002-penpot-design-source/dom-dumps/_probe/_probe-browser-route.json`

**2. The scanner opens, and the harness records the wrong screen — `node run-capture.mjs --dir _probe --spec …/probe-qr2.json`** (state 1 = Home baseline, state 2 = Home + click `aria-label ^Scan$`):
```

  FAILED _probe-qr-open-nodark — identical to "_probe-qr-baseline-home": the steps ran and
  threw nothing but the screen never changed (fp adc6bd013e40967b-53)
```
Both `expect` strings (`"Scan QR"`, `"Point camera at a QR code"`) *passed* — the assertion layer saw the scanner. The dump did not contain one node of it. This is the whole finding.

**3. Why — `node _probe-qr-chain.mjs`** walks from the "Scan QR" title up to `document.body`:
```
{"i":0,"tag":"DIV","w":0,"h":0,"x":835,"y":475,"display":"block","position":"static"}
{"i":1,"tag":"DIV","w":1280,"h":950,"position":"fixed"}
{"i":2,"tag":"DIV","w":1280,"h":0,"display":"flex","position":"relative"}

...
```

i=0 (0×0) and i=2 (1280×0) are both below `minSize: 2`, and neither is `display: contents`, so the pass-through at `extract-dom-layout.js:145` doesn't rescue them. `extractLayout({root: portal})` returns a single childless node `· [-445 -53 1280 950]` — rooting alone does not fix it, because i=2 still stops the descent.

unreachable: O/qr-scanner/scanning-native — IMPOSSIBLE in a web capture, no remedy. Everything that distinguishes this state is compiled out on web: NativeCamera (expo-camera's CameraView), the animated ScanLine (`Platform.OS === 'web' ? null : <NativeScanLine />`, QRScanner.tsx:187), the ZoomSlider (`showZoom = cameraReady && Platform.OS !== 'web'`, :510) and the camera-switch button (`{Platform.OS !== 'web' && …}`, :619). Platform.OS is a build constant with no runtime switch. Only an iOS/Android capture can produce it — which is out of scope for this harness.

O/qr-scanner/permission — IMPOSSIBLE in a web capture, no remedy, and the state does not exist on web at all. The permission screen ('Camera access is needed to scan QR codes.' + Grant Permission / Open Settings) is inside NativeCamera behind `!permission?.granted` (QRScanner.tsx:321-339). WebCamera has no permission UI whatsoever — it swallows the getUserMedia rejection in an empty `.catch(() => {})` (:246). Proven: with the camera blocked, body text was '… | Scan QR | Point camera at a QR code' and the rendered-button list was close + image-picker only, with no permission copy anywhere. Suggested replacement board: O/qr-scanner/web-camera-denied — the black viewfinder with the torch affordance absent, which IS the web behaviour when the camera is refused.

O/browser-consent/favicon — IMPOSSIBLE in a web capture, no remedy. `/browser` short-circuits at src/app/browser.tsx:364 (`if (!isWalletWebViewSupported) return <Fallback>`) because src/modules/webview/index.tsx:31 restricts the native WebView to iOS/Android, so the consent AppModal at :498 never mounts. Proven by capture: the entire dump of /browser?url=… is the single text node 'The in-app browser is only available on iOS and Android.'. Even past that gate the state is favicon-driven — `nav?.favicon`, set only by onNavigationChange, an event only the native view emits.

O/browser-consent/fallback-logo — IMPOSSIBLE in a web capture, no remedy. Same short-circuit as above. This state is the else-branch of the same expression (`logoUri && !consentLogoBroken`, browser.tsx:502-511): it needs a page whose captured favicon is absent AND whose /favicon.ico fails to load, both of which require a real navigation and a real image error from the native WebView.

O/browser-error/default — IMPOSSIBLE in a web capture, no remedy. The error overlay (browser.tsx:415-427) is gated on `loadError = nav?.error`, and `nav` is only ever populated by the native WebView's onNavigationChange. On web WalletWebView renders null (`if (!NativeWalletWebView) return null`, modules/webview/index.tsx:130) and the route never gets past the unsupported Fallback anyway.

O/qr-scanner/scanning-web — REACHABLE in the app and fully characterised, but NOT capturable by run-capture.mjs as it stands, so I am not claiming it as proven-through-the-real-harness. The blocker is plumbing, not platform: the react-native <Modal> portals under 0x0 / 1280x0 wrappers that extract-dom-layout.js:154 prunes before descending, so the harness recorded the Home board instead (fp adc6bd013e40967b-53, caught by differsFrom). Remedy proven end-to-end: forward per-state extract options ({minSize: 0}) + a 390x844 group viewport + chromium fake-camera flags. The recipe in spec_json is ready to run the moment those land, and fails loudly on differsFrom until then.

O/qr-scanner/torch-on — same status as scanning-web. Additionally needs the camera flags for its own sake: the torch button only exists once cameraReady fires, so on the stock launcher there is nothing to click and the step would throw 'no element for {"act":"click","label":"flashlight"}'. With the flags the button renders and the toggled board differs from scanning-web by exactly one property (the chip's bg #FFFFFF), fingerprints 79dd72c6089ba17c-65 vs 1165960b1158caf1-65.

sets.group: Settings overlays — O/language-picker, O/format-picker, O/add-network, O/network-editor, O/endpoint-editor, O/rpc-providers (15 cells, all on page "08 Overlays")
sets.summary:
All 15 planned cells are reachable and every one was captured through the real harness. None were "genuinely absent" as surfaces — what was absent was a working recipe. state-specs-5.json's `/settings` group already contained steps for 13 of them, but not one carried an `expect`, `forbid` or `differsFrom`, and none had ever produced a board.

Key authoring decisions, each forced by something the probe run found:

1. **`/parallel` priming group first.** run-capture launches a fresh browser, so `/settings` alone renders the empty real wallet. A zero-state `/parallel` group (settle 12000) arms parallel space for the `/settings` group that follows in the same browser — matching `settings-root` / `settings-advanced`, which were themselves shot in parallel space.

2. **Escape, not remount, between sub-flows.** The old recipes prepended `goto /wallet -> goto /settings` before each sub-flow (~4 s each) purely to dismiss the previous modal. A synthetic Escape does it and leaves the ADVANCED collapsible open, so one `click Advanced` serves four modals. Verified: after each Escape the previous modal's strings are gone from `document.body.innerText`.

3. **`differsFrom` anchored on siblings + two boards already on disk.** My first draft chained each state's `differsFrom` to the previous unrelated state; one genuine failure then cascaded into 13 "no fingerprint available" failures. Each family's first state now names `settings-root` or `settings-advanced` (both resolve on disk — `dom-dumps/pruned/settings-root.json` fp `afc2c6d4d04b4cae-89`, `dom-dumps/screens/settings-advanced.json` fp `91c5aa9fbae2c935-110`), which is the meaningful check anyway: it proves the modal opened rather than the board being a re-dump of the screen underneath.

4. **`O/endpoint-editor/health-error-states` needed a mechanism that did not exist in the older recipe.** `handleSave` is blur-only and the harness never focuses an input, so typing a bad URL alone changes no badge. But `onChangeText` writes `endpoints` state immediately, and the health effect's other dependency is `refreshCount` — bumped by the header RefreshCw. Driving that gives all four `ServiceHealthBadge` outcomes in one board (`HTTPS required` / `Offline` / `237ms` / `No rates returned`), which is what the manifest's own drift note asks for. The RefreshCw has no text and no aria-label, so it is `clickNth n: 24` — documented as fragile, with the `expect` list as the guard (hitting 23 opens a tab and never refreshes; hitting 25 closes the modal; either way the state fails without writing).

Three app/plan findings worth recording:
- **`O/add-network/result` no longer shows the incompatible variant.** state-specs-5's note (and the manifest drift note) assumed Celo would come back incompatible so the "Open Chain Setup Tool / Re-check" block would be drawn inside the result board. Celo Mainnet is now fully compatible — all 11 contracts + P256 — so the board carries the accent "Add Network" CTA instead. The incompatible variant is now depicted nowhere; it needs a second board or an explicit exclusion.
- **Three AddNetworkModal error strings are hardcoded English, not i18n**: `This network is already added` (SettingsScreen.tsx:623), `Chain {id} not found` (:630), `No RPC endpoint available for this network` (:642).
- **`EXPLORER` health reads "Offline" from the capture browser** (etherscan.io is not fetchable, even no-cors), so `network-editor/card-expanded` honestly carries one ok badge and one error badge. The assertion is a pattern (`\d+\s*ms|offline`), never a latency.

Three assertion traps that will bite anyone writing in this area, all documented inline in the notes: the space-grouped number example uses **U+00A0**, not a space (`expect: "1 234 567,89"` fails — use `expectRe`); **`Alchemy`** cannot be forbidden because "Alchemy, dRPC, Ankr keys" is the RPC Providers *row subtitle* behind every modal; and **`Test`** cannot be forbidden because the parallel-space badge renders "mock passkey · test". Likewise `EXPLORER` cannot be forbidden on `network-editor/collapsed` — "RPC, Explorer & Bundler URLs" is on screen behind it — so `RPC URL` is the collapsed/expanded discriminator.

Nothing was committed, no canonical dump was touched, and manifest.json was not edited. The API key typed into the Alchemy field never reaches the dump (secureTextEntry) — `grep vela-design-capture-invalid-key` over all 15 dumps returns nothing.

I read all 25 sources and ran a census of real JSX render sites (excluding tests and the design gallery). The gap is not 25 missing components — it is a modelling error. Applying one rule ("a library family earns its entry if it has 2+ render sites, or is a shared frame/primitive others compose; otherwise it is a surface — board it and record the family cell as an exclusion"), 13 of the 25 deserve a library family, 11 should be boards only, and 1 should be excluded outright.

KEEP AS FAMILIES (13): AppAlert (1 mount, ~40 showAlert call sites), AccountSwitcherModal (3 hosts), AddTokenPanel (2 hosts — it exists precisely to be a chrome-less body), BugReportModal (2), CurrencySheet (2, and its `title` prop exists only because of the second), IdenticonViewerSheet (1 JSX site but 5 provider mounts), NetworkFilterSheet (2), RpcFixForm (2 — the clearest case in the list), SigningSheet (3), ScreenContainer (11), ConnectionFlowStates (2, by explicit design), QRScanner (4), FlowArrowSend (2).

BOARDS ONLY (11): BalanceDetailSheet, BrowserHistorySheet, BundlerFundingView, ConnectionEventDetailSheet, TransactionDetailSheet, TreasuryBootstrapSheet, BatchImportSheet, ContactPicker, ContactsManager, ExtensionSignSheet, HoldingsList — each has exactly ONE render site. All of them already have, or are already planned to have, O/* or S/* boards; 18 of the 20 sheets already have a committed dump in dom-dumps/overlays/. Two of them are not sheets at all: HoldingsList is Home's Assets tab, ExtensionSignSheet is a root-mounted controller whose sheet is a private inline View.
